text:
JJ Peterka's first season in Boston is quietly the role he has been waiting for. He is playing 17:39 a night, up from just under 16 last season in Utah, and he has 13 points in 17 games. His own chances are up too: 1.06 expected goals per 60 minutes, from 0.73. That combination is why our numbers flag him as a breakout candidate, with the caveat that 17 games is not much.

What we like is that the goals haven't really arrived yet. He has 4 on 5.32 expected, shooting 12.9 percent, a touch under league average. Lately he has been the passer, with two-assist nights against San Jose, Chicago and Pittsburgh in his last ten. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he exits his own zone with possession 59 percent of the time, which helps a team that has had trouble breaking out.

Our range puts him around 58 points for the season. If the finishing catches up with the chances, the upper end looks reachable.
headline: Peterka is getting the minutes he never got before
